scope: read-only exact-input equivalence for the previously measured core, deep, performance, and storage lanes

coreInputEquivalence.oracle: The complete c47 to f6 manifest diff contains no root Cargo, dakia-core, fuzz, mail-parser, lettre, or core test-data path.
coreInputEquivalence.conclusion: The Rust core and vendored parser/SMTP inputs exercised by the c47 source run are byte-identical in f6. This does not carry forward the c47 native desktop checks because apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs changed.

deepInputEquivalence.oracle: The deep lane invokes only mail-safety-servers.sh and run-mail-safety-fuzz.sh. Neither those entrypoints nor their core, fuzz, fixture, Cargo, or vendor inputs are among the three changed paths.
deepInputEquivalence.conclusion: The recorded c47 independent-server and bounded fuzz inputs are byte-identical in f6. This is an input-equivalence result, not another fuzz or independent-server execution.

performanceInputEquivalence.oracle: The runner, root Cargo resolution, dakia-core implementation and manual resilience/performance tests are unchanged. All three changed files are outside this lane.
performanceInputEquivalence.conclusion: The prior c47 mailbox-scale and resource-soak measurements retain byte-equivalent production and runner inputs in f6. Matching inputs does not prove identical timing, code generation, system load, or incremental-cache state.

storageCoverageInputEquivalence.conclusion: Every root Cargo, dakia-core, mail-parser, and lettre input recorded for the three separate storage coverage cohorts remains byte-identical in f6.

limitations: This report performs path-and-content equivalence checks. It does not rerun source, core, deep, fuzz, performance, coverage, native, provider, or packaged-app lanes.
The f6 source snapshot is not wholly equivalent to c47. Native desktop lib.rs and two native fixture harness files changed, so prior native and whole-source claims are not carried forward here.
The deep result retains the recorded bounded fuzz limits and their temporal-safety limitation. It does not establish the absence of all parser failures.
The performance result remains tied to its recorded hardware, build profile, and load conditions.
The storage result remains three separate focused cohorts. Branch observations are not aggregated into product or workspace coverage.
